Which molecules belong to the same homologous series?

intelligence.enrichment: A compound is formed from elements whose particles are tightly attached; its properties are different from those of the elements forming it, and its constituent elements cannot be separated by any physical method. Chemical joining creates a new substance, so the compound no longer shows the separate properties of its elements and cannot be separated by ordinary physical processes. The learner correctly applies this rule: A compound is formed from elements whose particles are tightly attached; its properties are different from those of the elements forming it, and its constituent elements cannot be separated by any physical method. A compound keeps the visible or useful properties of the elements inside it.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Elements, compounds and mixtures. The student must decide: Classify a substance as a compound when different elements are chemically joined and the substance has properties different from those elements.
